_comment: Copy to acl.json (gitignored, chmod 600) and edit. The values below are examples.
A principal is a person or a room — never a bot. Which bot is on the other
end is a deployment detail, and swapping it must not touch this file.
apiKey: never share one between two consumers. The key is the identity, and
the audit log records the name it resolves to. Generate with:
openssl rand -hex 24
role: read | write | admin.
read  — search, fetch, list labels.
write — everything above, plus creating and correcting places, entries and
photos. Deliberately stops short of deleting a place or renaming
one: not because they are dangerous — git remembers — but because
they are rare, and a rarely needed capability is better asked for
than left lying around.
admin — everything, including re-rendering and reindexing.
allow / deny: adjust the role for one principal. deny wins over allow.
A denied operation is not merely refused when called: it is left out of what
GET /me reports, so a client built from that list never learns it exists.
The operation names are the ones in acl.ts. A name that matches none of them
is warned about at boot — a typo in a deny list looks like a control and is
none.

intake._comment: Photos arrive before anyone knows where they belong, so the upload needs no more than this.

painel._comment: A read-only consumer: a dashboard, a map, a static export.
